cases.sentence: По моему мнению, действовать на ___ может только тот, который имеет высшее развитие, который…
cases.explain: «другой народ» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “It seems to me,” Alexey Alexandrovitch said languidly, and with no haste, “that that’s the same thing. In my opinion, influence over another people is only possible to the people which has the higher development, which. …”

cases.sentence: Мы видим, что Рейн офранцузился, а немцы не ниже стоят! – кричал он. – Тут есть ___!
cases.explain: «другой закон» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But that’s just the question,” Pestsov broke in in his bass. He was always in a hurry to speak, and seemed always to put his whole soul into what he was saying. “In what are we to make higher development consist? The English, the French, the Germans, which is at the highest stage of development? Which of them will nationalize the other? We see the Rhine provinces have been turned French, but the Germans are not at a lower stage!” he shouted. “There is another law at work there.”

cases.sentence: – Мне кажется, что влияние всегда на стороне ___, – сказал Алексей Александрович, слегка поднимая брови.
cases.explain: «истинного образования» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I fancy that the greater influence is always on the side of true civilization,” said Alexey Alexandrovitch, slightly lifting his eyebrows.

cases.sentence: – Но в чем же мы должны полагать признаки ___? – сказал Песцов.
cases.explain: «истинного образования» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “But what are we to lay down as the outward signs of true civilization?” said Pestsov.

cases.sentence: Я не вижу ___, почему классическим наукам дано преимущество пред реальными.
cases.explain: «ясных доводов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I am not expressing my own opinion of either form of culture,” Sergey Ivanovitch said, holding out his glass with a smile of condescension, as to a child. “I only say that both sides have strong arguments to support them,” he went on, addressing Alexey Alexandrovitch. “My sympathies are classical from education, but in this discussion I am personally unable to arrive at a conclusion. I see no distinct grounds for classical studies being given a preeminence over scientific studies.”

cases.sentence: – Я не могу вполне с этим согласиться, – отвечал Алексей Александрович. – Мне кажется, что нельзя не признать того, что ___ изучения форм языков особенно благотворно действует на духовное развитие.
cases.explain: «самый процесс» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I cannot quite agree with that,” responded Alexey Alexandrovitch. “It seems to me that one must admit that the very process of studying the forms of language has a peculiarly favorable influence on intellectual development. Moreover, it cannot be denied that the influence of the classical authors is in the highest degree moral, while, unfortunately, with the study of the natural sciences are associated the false and noxious doctrines which are the curse of our day.”

cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович хотел что-то сказать, но Песцов своим ___ перебил его.
cases.explain: «густым басом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Sergey Ivanovitch would have said something, but Pestsov interrupted him in his rich bass. He began warmly contesting the justice of this view. Sergey Ivanovitch waited serenely to speak, obviously with a convincing reply ready.

cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович спокойно дожидался слова, очевидно с готовым ___.
cases.explain: «победительным возражением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Sergey Ivanovitch would have said something, but Pestsov interrupted him in his rich bass. He began warmly contesting the justice of this view. Sergey Ivanovitch waited serenely to speak, obviously with a convincing reply ready.

cases.sentence: Но теперь мы знаем, что в этих пилюлях классического образования лежит ___ антинигилизма, и мы смело предлагаем их нашим пациентам…
cases.explain: «целебная сила» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “If it had not been for the distinctive property of anti-nihilistic influence on the side of classical studies, we should have considered the subject more, have weighed the arguments on both sides,” said Sergey Ivanovitch with a subtle smile, “we should have given elbow-room to both tendencies. But now we know that these little pills of classical learning possess the medicinal property of anti-nihilism, and we boldly prescribe them to our patients. … But what if they had no such medicinal property?” he wound up humorously.

cases.sentence: Правительство, очевидно, руководствуется ___, оставаясь индифферентным к влияниям, которые могут иметь принимаемые меры.
cases.explain: «общими соображениями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I can’t agree even,” said he, “that the government had that aim. The government obviously is guided by abstract considerations, and remains indifferent to the influence its measures may exercise. The education of women, for instance, would naturally be regarded as likely to be harmful, but the government opens schools and universities for women.”

cases.sentence: Например, вопрос женского образования должен бы был считаться зловредным, но правительство открывает ___ и университеты.
cases.explain: «женские курсы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I can’t agree even,” said he, “that the government had that aim. The government obviously is guided by abstract considerations, and remains indifferent to the influence its measures may exercise. The education of women, for instance, would naturally be regarded as likely to be harmful, but the government opens schools and universities for women.”
